submission.justification:
Crystal-K3 at 4.0 cm thickness achieves the best possible energy resolution of 2.894% FWHM at 662 keV for the low-background screening facility. This configuration was identified through a systematic 18-simulation optimization campaign spanning the full allowed thickness range (2-10 cm) and all three candidate crystals.

CRYSTAL SELECTION: Crystal-K3 outperforms alternatives by substantial margins - 36.7% better resolution than Crystal-K2 (4.568% at 6 cm) and 66.2% better than Crystal-K1 (8.569% at 6 cm). The high light yield and fast decay time of K3 provide optimal photon statistics and timing characteristics for energy resolution.

THICKNESS OPTIMIZATION: Fine-tuned simulations identified a robust optimal plateau at 4.0-4.2 cm, both achieving 2.894% FWHM. Thinner crystals show degraded resolution (3.8 cm: 2.954%, 3.0 cm: 3.116%, 2.0 cm: 3.368%) due to incomplete light collection, while thicker crystals degrade progressively (4.5 cm: 2.921%, 6 cm: 2.928%, 8 cm: 3.451%, 10 cm: 4.043%) due to self-absorption and light attenuation effects.

LOW-BACKGROUND SUITABILITY: The superior 2.894% energy resolution is critical for the facility's assay program, enabling better peak identification in complex spectra, improved peak-to-background discrimination, and enhanced sensitivity for screening construction materials. The fast decay time prevents pulse pileup while maintaining high throughput. Crystal-K3 is compatible with the facility's shielding configuration (20 cm lead + 5 cm OFHC copper + radon purge) and DAQ system (250 MS/s, 14-bit ADC).

MANUFACTURING ROBUSTNESS: The 4.0-4.2 cm optimal plateau provides ±0.1 cm manufacturing tolerance while maintaining peak performance. The crystal is available from vendors in required sizes for Q2 procurement, supporting the Q3 commissioning and Q4 first assays timeline.
